The ending of the story feels completely natural and earned because it brings all the narrative threads, character arcs, and central themes to a poignant, unified climax. Throughout the story, the narrator (Clara) navigates her awkwardness as a teenager, her search for belonging, and the unspoken, impending loss of her terminally ill father. The final scene at the "White Party" directly addresses why her father brought her on the cruise in the first place: to show her "how people take care of one another" and to reassure himself that she will be able to find her own community after he is gone. Furthermore, the final paragraph visually ties together all the significant characters she connected with on the journey (her father, Gregory, Simon, Bear, and Mateo), providing a deeply satisfying sense of emotional closure and resonance rather than an abrupt stop.
